newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-SPAIN LOOK TO SEAL GROUP AND END CZECH HOPES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SPAIN LOOK TO SEAL GROUP AND END CZECH HOPES.

text.p: Spain and the Czech Republic could hardly go into Sunday's World Cup qualifying match in more contrasting positions.

While a win would leave Spain poised to win group six, even three points may not be enough for the Czechs, who face an early exit from the competition less than a year after reaching the Euro 96 final.
With only four points from as many games, defeat or a draw would certainly drop the Czechs from contention.
Spain lead the group after five wins and away draws against the Yugoslavs and the Czechs.
But anything less than a victory on Sunday could again open the way to Yugoslavia, who are one point behind Spain with 16 points after snatching a last-gasp victory from the Czechs in April.
The result left Czech coach Dusan Uhrin realistic about his side's chances.
"This is our last chance, if we win, we are still playing for a spot," Uhrin said.
To make matters worse for the Czechs, injuries have left Uhrin struggling to put together a side.
The Czechs were already having to plug a gaping hole in midfield through the suspension of Atletico Madrid set-piece ace Radek Bejbl and an injury suffered by Liverpool's Patrik Berger.

But Uhrin's problems were exacerbated on Wednesday when Kaiserslautern striker Pavel Kuka and Racing Strasbourg defender Jan Suchoparek, mainstays of the Czech team for the past two years, also pulled out injured.
Kuka, who has been heavily criticised for missing several easy chances in the last two games, will be replaced up front by Racing Lens striker Vladimir Smicer.
Sigma Olomouc defender Karel Rada is expected to replace Suchoparek.
"I will not call up any other players. We have right now exactly 19 players who will be able to travel to Spain ... and I hope nothing else happens to anyone," Uhrin said.
Javier Clemente's Spain side also have injury problems.
Defenders Sergi Barjuan and Miguel Angel Nadal have both pulled out of the squad, while another Barcelona man, midfielder Guillermo Amor is doubtful for the game because of 'flu.
Clemente has brought in striker Ismael Urzaiz and utility player Juan Lopez to fill the gaps.
Poor weather has further disrupted Spain's preparations, heavy rain even causing the partial collapse of the ceiling during one of Clemente's press conferences.
But Clemente is confident the team will not be affected.
"The base of the team is already there," said Clemente "And if we beat the Czechs then World Cup classification will be a fact, because we then have games against not so strong rivals,"
"I believe we can win, the Czechs are not easy rivals, but my team is strong," he said.
Probable teams:
Spain:
Goalkeeper - Andoni Zubizarreta
Defenders - Rafael Alkorta, Roberto Rios, Juan Lopez, Abelardo Fernandez
Midfielders - Fernando Hierro, Josep Guardiola, Julen Guerrero, Emilio Amavisca
Strikers - Alfonso Perez, Raul Gonzalez
